result.target_summary: The platform is founded on GPUs for parallel workloads, expanded in fiscal year 2022 to include DPUs and in fiscal year 2024 to include CPUs, allowing optimization across the computing, networking, and storage stack.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures describe the hardware foundation of the accelerated computing platform. D020 identifies GPUs as the foundation, available in industry servers and DGX supercomputers, with reference designs (HGX, EGX, etc.). D018 identifies GPUs as the foundation for parallel workloads, available in industry standard servers, and notes the platform's expansion to include DPUs and CPUs. The core subject is the composition of the hardware platform foundation (GPUs primarily, with specific system implementations).

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Product Portfolio and Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: The Data Center segment includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products. The company leverages these technologies to address computational, visual data processing, and AI workload acceleration needs by enabling optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose that their accelerated computing platforms are founded on multiple hardware types including CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs to optimize data center workloads. NVDA explicitly states that the platform foundation includes GPUs, expanded to include DPUs in fiscal 2022 and CPUs in fiscal 2024. Similarly, AMD's Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, and DPUs, noting that different combinations of these components enable optimization of performance and power for diverse workloads.

sentences.text: Beyond GPUs, our data center platform expanded to include DPUs in fiscal year 2022 and CPUs in fiscal year 2024.
We can optimize across the entire computing, networking and storage stack to deliver data center-scale computing solutions.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server-class CPUs, GPUs, AI accelerators, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoC products.
Different combinations of CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, SmartNICs, and Adaptive SoCs enable the optimization of performance and power for a diverse set of workloads.
